authority: diagnostic: paper only, not investment advice
flags: Encore issued a notice calling all outstanding 4.00% Convertible Senior Notes due 2029 for redemption. The nine-month cash flow statement shows a payment to settle convertible senior notes of 367,855 (table in thousands).

In the nine months ended September 30, 2026 the company shows a debt refinancing. It took in 1,128,676 from senior secured notes and repaid 983,540 of senior secured notes (table in thousands), and it recorded a loss on extinguishment of debt of 30,533 (table in thousands).
In its third quarter earnings release the company raised its full-year 2026 guidance for portfolio purchases, collections and EPS. The new EPS range is $15.50 to $16.00 per share.

business_model.claim: Encore buys portfolios of defaulted consumer receivables at deep discounts to face value and earns money by collecting on them from the consumers.
quotes: We primarily purchase portfolios of defaulted consumer receivables at deep discounts to face value

business_model.claim: The sellers are credit originators such as banks, credit unions, consumer finance companies and retailers. The people paying are the defaulted consumers. In Europe the company also services non-performing loans for originators for a fee.
quotes: Defaulted receivables are consumers’ unpaid financial obligations to credit originators, including banks, credit unions, consumer finance companies and commercial retailers.
Servicing revenue consists primarily of fee-based income earned on accounts collected on behalf of others, primarily credit originators.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited MD&A. The filings call them business units, and the excerpt does not show formal segment reporting.
business_model.claim: The business is organized into three units: MCM (United States), Cabot (Europe and the UK) and LAAP (Latin America and Asia-Pacific). LAAP has not been significant to consolidated results.
quotes: To date, operating results from LAAP have not been significant to our total consolidated operating results.

business_model.claim: Revenue is mostly debt purchasing revenue. In Q3 2026 that was 525,457 of 544,541 total revenues (table in thousands). Servicing revenue was 17,474 and other revenues were 1,610.

business_model.basis: the accretion mechanism is stated in the 10-K. The link between the larger balance and higher revenue is inferred from the cited figures.
business_model.claim: Portfolio revenue is the accretion of the discount on the receivable balance, roughly the balance times the effective interest rate. It rises with the size of the receivable portfolio balance, which depends on how much was purchased in recent years.
quotes: Portfolio revenue, which is the accretion of the discount on the negative allowance due to the passage of time (generally the receivable portfolio balance multiplied by the EIR)

business_model.claim: Purchase volume is a key driver and is concentrated in the U.S. U.S. purchases were 309,953 in Q3 2026 against 261,140 a year earlier, and 998,024 for nine months against 894,770 (table in thousands). Europe purchases were 79,702 against 84,929 in the quarter.
quotes: The majority of our deployments in the U.S. come from forward flow agreements, and the timing, contract duration, and volumes for each contract can fluctuate leading to variation when comparing to prior periods.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-Q MD&A, with the counter-argument from the 10-K risk factors
business_model.claim: Supply and pricing in the U.S. are described as favorable, though pricing in Q3 was slightly higher than in prior quarters. In Europe competitive pricing limits how much capital is deployed.
quotes: With market supply remaining elevated, pricing in the third quarter remained at favorable levels, although portfolio pricing was slightly higher compared to prior quarters.
In general, portfolio pricing remains competitive across our European footprint, constraining the amount of capital we elect to deploy in Europe.

business_model.claim: Collections are what the revenue is built on. Total collections from purchased receivables were 753,845 in Q3 2026 against 663,018 a year earlier. The U.S. contributed 588,786 and Europe 164,084 (table in thousands).
quotes: The increases in collections in the United States were primarily a result of consistent increases in capital deployments and enhanced collection strategies in the United States in recent periods.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K MD&A and the 10-Q income statement (amounts in thousands)
business_model.claim: Changes in recoveries make reported revenue volatile. They were 208,771 for 2025 against (89,740) for 2024, and 244,898 for the first nine months of 2026 against 140,699.
quotes: Recoveries above or below forecast represent over and under-performance in the reporting period, respectively and are expected to vary from period to period.

business_model.basis: the mechanism is stated in the 10-K. The Q3 figures come from the 10-Q.
business_model.claim: A large share of collections goes through the legal channel, and its cost is a main cost driver. Cost of legal collections was 100,400 in Q3 2026 against 80,010 a year earlier. U.S. legal collections were 219,444 against 170,545 (table in thousands).
quotes: The increase in cost of legal collections during the year ended December 31, 2025, compared to the year ended December 31, 2024, was primarily due to increased legal placements in this channel in the United States.

business_model.claim: Part of revenue depends on winning court judgments against consumers, so changes in court practice or costs affect the business.
quotes: We generate a significant portion of our revenue by collecting on judgments that are granted by courts in lawsuits filed against consumers.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K MD&A for the annual driver. The Q3 figures are from the income statement.
business_model.claim: Staff cost is the largest operating expense, and it rises with wages and collection performance. Salaries and employee benefits were 117,470 in Q3 2026 against 117,118 a year earlier (table in thousands).
quotes: The increase in salaries and employee benefits during the year ended December 31, 2025, compared to the year ended December 31, 2024, was primarily driven by a general increase in wages and higher account manager compensation as a result of higher collection performance.

business_model.basis: figures are stated. The funding role of debt is inferred from the balance sheet and the cash flow statement.
business_model.claim: The business is largely debt-funded, and interest is a large cost. Borrowings were 4,237,800 against receivable portfolios, net of 4,763,412 and total assets of 5,682,707 at September 30, 2026 (table in thousands). Q3 interest expense was 72,299.

business_model.basis: stated in the cash flow statement. The explanation is inferred from the reconciliation lines.
business_model.claim: Reported profit is above operating cash flow because changes in recoveries are non-cash. In the first nine months of 2026 net income was 274,255 and operating cash flow 159,630. Purchases of receivable portfolios were 1,187,072 and collections applied to portfolios were 1,004,448 (table in thousands).

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K and the cash flow statement
business_model.claim: Management lists capital priorities as portfolio purchases, share repurchases and possible M&A. Repurchases were 73,993 in the first nine months of 2026 (table in thousands).
quotes: Our capital allocation priorities include portfolio purchases at attractive returns, the return of capital to stockholders through share repurchases and the consideration of strategic merger and acquisition (M&A).

business_model.claim: Servicing revenue is a small, fee-based line from Europe and has been shrinking. It was 17,474 in Q3 2026 against 22,175 a year earlier (table in thousands).
quotes: We also provide debt servicing and other portfolio management services to credit originators for non-performing loans in Europe.

competitive_position.basis: Stated by the company in P1 and P4; not independently evidenced.
competitive_position.claim: Encore describes itself as a market leader in US portfolio purchasing and recovery through MCM, and as one of the largest credit management services providers in Europe and the UK through Cabot. These are its two primary operations. This is the company's own characterisation, not a measured market share.
quotes: Through MCM, we are a market leader in portfolio purchasing and recovery in the United States.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A and the earnings release.
competitive_position.claim: Collections show strong momentum. Q3 2026 collections from purchased receivables rose to $753.8 million, up 13.7%. Nine-month collections were $2,209.1 million, up 14.9%. US collections grew faster than Europe's: $588,786 versus $501,768 in Q3 for the US, and $164,084 versus $160,329 for Europe (tables in thousands).
quotes: Collections from purchased receivables increased by $90.8 million, or 13.7%, to $753.8 million during the three months ended September 30, 2026, as compared to $663.0 million during the three months ended September 30, 2025.

competitive_position.claim: US purchasing supply is robust and pricing favorable, and Encore is deploying more capital there. Q3 US purchases were $309,953 versus $261,140 (table in thousands). Management says pricing was slightly higher than in prior quarters.
quotes: With lending and charge-off rates remaining near recent peak levels, U.S. portfolio supply continues to be robust.

competitive_position.basis: Stated by management in the 10-K; effect on returns is inferred from the stated mechanism.
competitive_position.claim: Encore attributes its advantage partly to data and analytics. It says success depends on an information and data advantage built on proprietary models. It credits new technologies and digital capabilities for US collections over-performance, which was concentrated in recent vintages.
quotes: We believe that success in our business depends on our ability to establish and maintain an information and data advantage.

The collections over-performance in the U.S. was driven by the deployment of new technologies, enhanced digital capabilities and continued operational innovation, which enabled us to reach more consumers, leading to more payments as well as a larger payer book.

competitive_position.basis: Figures stated in F2; the dependence is inferred from the revenue lines.
competitive_position.claim: Earnings lean on changes in recoveries, which are forecast revisions and over-performance rather than steady accretion. In Q3 2026 they were $111,043 against $63,636 a year earlier (table in thousands), within total revenues of $544,541. Portfolio revenue was $414,414.

competitive_position.basis: Management belief and statements in the 10-K and 10-Q; not independently verified.
competitive_position.claim: Compliance credentials and scale are presented as a moat. MCM says it has certification from all major US issuers. Management believes smaller competitors face difficulties from regulatory pressure and rising capital costs, which favors larger participants.
quotes: MCM has achieved certification from all major U.S. issuers who sell their charged-off accounts to third parties.
We believe that smaller competitors continue to face difficulties in the portfolio purchasing market because of the high cost to operate due to regulatory pressure and increasing cost of capital.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A; the earnings release describes Cabot as a solid quarter.
competitive_position.claim: Europe is a weaker part of the position. Cabot's Q3 purchases were $79,702 versus $84,929 a year earlier (table in thousands), and management says competitive pricing constrains capital deployment there. Cabot's Q3 collections were roughly flat to modestly higher.
quotes: Pricing continues to remain competitive in our European footprint, constraining the amount of capital we choose to deploy in Europe.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 10-K risk factors; the 10-Q (P5) says there is no material change.
competitive_position.claim: Intense competition for portfolios is a named threat. Bids are won mainly on price, and competitors may pay prices Encore finds uneconomic or have cheaper financing. That could force lower returns or lower volumes.
quotes: The charged-off receivables purchasing market is highly competitive.

Some of our competitors may obtain alternative sources of financing at more favorable rates than those available to us, the proceeds from which may be used to fund expansion and to increase the amount of charged-off receivables they purchase.

competitive_position.claim: Seller concentration and forward flow terms are named supply threats. A few large sellers can account for a big share of purchases, and forward flow contracts can lock in prices above spot in falling markets. Terminating them may be possible only in limited circumstances.
quotes: A significant portion of our portfolio purchases during any period may be concentrated with a small number of sellers, which could adversely affect our volume and timing of purchases.

competitive_position.basis: Figures from the 10-Q and F2; the cost-pressure link is stated in the 10-K risk factors.
competitive_position.claim: Collections increasingly run through the higher-cost legal channel, which is both an advantage in reach and a cost and dependence risk. US legal collections were $219,444 versus $170,545 in Q3 (table in thousands). Cost of legal collections was $100,400 versus $80,010 (table in thousands).
quotes: A significant portion of our collections relies upon our success in individual lawsuits brought against consumers and our ability to collect on judgments in our favor.

competitive_position.basis: Figures stated in the statements and the 8-K; the competitive link is inferred from the competitor-financing risk factor.
competitive_position.claim: Leverage and funding cost are a structural exposure. Borrowings were $4,237,800 against stockholders' equity of $1,078,682 (table in thousands), and Q3 interest expense was $72,299. Encore refinanced during 2026, with a $30,533 loss on extinguishment of debt in the nine months. It called its 4.00% Convertible Senior Notes due 2029 for redemption.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 10-K risk factors; the regulatory section is truncated in the packet.
competitive_position.claim: Macroeconomic, bankruptcy and regulatory conditions are named threats to collectability and operations. Consumer financial stress, rising bankruptcy filings and expanding regulation could reduce collections or raise costs.
quotes: Our business, financial condition and operating results may be adversely affected if consumer bankruptcy filings increase or if bankruptcy laws change.
Our business is subject to extensive laws and regulations, which have increased and may continue to increase.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the earnings release; it shows management expectations only.
competitive_position.claim: Management is confident enough to raise 2026 guidance, which supports the current momentum. Global collections are now expected at $2.90 billion to $2.95 billion, and EPS at $15.50 to $16.00.
quotes: Given the strength and momentum of our business, we are raising our full-year 2026 guidance.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the balance sheet (F1) and the earnings release VIE note (P6). The point about earmarked cash comes from the P6 note. How much of the 158,425 is freely available is inferred and not stated.
financial_health.claim: Cash on hand is small relative to the balance sheet: cash and cash equivalents were 158,425 at Sep 30, 2026 against 156,784 at Dec 31, 2025 (table in thousands), within total assets of 5,682,707. Of the cash, 48,558 sits in consolidated variable interest entities.
quotes: Most assets in the table below include those assets that can only be used to settle obligations of consolidated VIEs.

financial_health.basis: Stated figures from the balance sheet (F1). The point that borrowings grew faster than equity is inferred from the printed figures without computing a ratio.
financial_health.claim: Leverage is high and rising. Borrowings were 4,237,800 at Sep 30, 2026 versus 4,001,293 at Dec 31, 2025, and total liabilities were 4,604,025 against stockholders' equity of 1,078,682 (table in thousands). Of the borrowings, 784,567 sit in consolidated VIEs.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the 10-K Item 1 (P1). The repurchase figure is from the cash flow statement (F3).
financial_health.claim: The company's own stated leverage policy ties capital allocation to a target leverage range, but the range itself is not given in the cited text.
quotes: Depending on our relative leverage and a number of other factors, we may apply excess cash toward reducing our debt or, in circumstances in which we are operating within our target leverage range or below the lower end of our target leverage range, we may allocate capital toward share repurchases.

financial_health.basis: Figures are stated in F2 and F3. The explanation of why the two measures differ is inferred from the cash flow line items and the 10-K description of changes in recoveries.
financial_health.claim: Operating cash flow was 159,630 for the nine months to Sep 30, 2026 versus 136,388 a year earlier, while net income was 274,255 versus 180,177 (table in thousands). Operating cash flow is much smaller than net income, partly because the 244,898 of changes in recoveries included in revenue is deducted as a non-cash item.

financial_health.basis: Stated in F2 and the MD&A tables (P3, P4). The point that the item is estimate-driven rests on the 10-K definition quoted.
financial_health.claim: Earnings quality is helped by collections, but a large part of recent profit is estimate-driven. Changes in recoveries were 244,898 over nine months versus 140,699 a year earlier and 111,043 in the quarter versus 63,636, against total revenues of 1,511,824 for the nine months (table in thousands).
quotes: Recoveries above or below forecast represent over and under-performance in the reporting period, respectively and are expected to vary from period to period.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the earnings release (P6) and the income statement (F2).
financial_health.claim: Non-GAAP Adjusted EBITDA was 644,320 for the nine months versus 489,449 a year earlier, and 245,171 in the third quarter versus 184,756 (table in thousands). Operating income was 601,499 versus 453,254, and interest expense was 219,256 versus 218,715.
quotes: Adjusted EBITDA has not been prepared in accordance with GAAP and should not be considered as an alternative to, or more meaningful than, net income and net income per share as indicators of the Company’s operating performance.

financial_health.basis: Stated line items in F3. The reading of the funding gap is inferred from those lines.
financial_health.claim: The company reinvests more than it collects against principal and funds the gap with debt. It purchased receivable portfolios of (1,187,072) while collections applied to receivable portfolios were 1,004,448, and cash paid for interest was 183,459 (table in thousands).

financial_health.basis: Stated in F2 and F3. The reading of this as a refinancing is inferred from the matched issuance and repayment lines and the extinguishment loss.
financial_health.claim: In the nine months to Sep 30, 2026 the company refinanced a large amount of debt: proceeds from senior secured notes were 1,128,676 against repayments of 983,540, and credit facility proceeds were 1,297,830 against repayments of 946,236 (table in thousands). The refinancing carried a loss on extinguishment of debt of (30,533) and refinancing costs of (39,830).

financial_health.basis: Redemption terms and the estimate are stated in P8. The settlement amounts are stated in F3 and P6. Linking the cash flow line to this redemption is inferred.
financial_health.claim: The 4.00% Convertible Senior Notes due 2029 were called for full redemption in the quarter just reported, with conversions to be settled in cash, so the convertible debt was met from cash and financing rather than left to its 2029 maturity. The company estimated roughly $332.5 million of cash settlement, and the cash flow statement shows payments to settle convertible senior notes of (367,855) and proceeds from convertible hedge instruments of 31,780 (table in thousands).
quotes: Notes that are converted after they are called for Redemption will be settled in cash.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the MD&A table (P4) and the earnings release (P6). Linking them to debt service is inferred.
financial_health.claim: How the remaining debt can be met rests on collections. Collections from purchased receivables were 753,845 in the third quarter and 2,209,123 for nine months (table in thousands), and estimated remaining collections were 10,451,677 against 9,489,772 a year earlier.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P4 (purchases table and explanation); the condition is inferred from P4 and the 10-K risk factors.
growth_thesis.claim: U.S. portfolio purchasing is the first driver. Third-quarter U.S. purchases were $309,953 (table in thousands), against $261,140 a year earlier. Management attributes the rise to robust supply and favorable pricing. For this to continue, issuer supply must stay elevated and portfolio pricing must stay at levels that allow acceptable returns.
quotes: The increases in portfolio purchases in the U.S. were driven by robust portfolio supply and pricing at favorable levels.

growth_thesis.basis: Balance and revenue figures are stated in F1, F2 and P4. The mechanism is stated in P3. The sustaining condition is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: A larger receivable portfolio base lifts portfolio revenue. Receivable portfolios, net rose to 4,763,412 (table in thousands) from 4,371,532 at year-end. Third-quarter portfolio revenue was $414,414 against $370,126. This continues only if purchases keep adding to the balance faster than collections run it off and the effective interest rate on new purchases holds up.
quotes: The increase in revenue recognized from portfolio basis during the year ended December 31, 2025, as compared to the year ended December 31, 2024, was primarily due to a higher portfolio basis (i.e. a higher receivable portfolios balance) in the U.S. driven by a consistent higher volume of purchases in recent years.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P3 and P4; that the effect depends on continued over-performance is inferred from P3's statement that such amounts vary.
growth_thesis.claim: Collections growth and recoveries above forecast are a second driver. Third-quarter collections were $753,845 against $663,018, and changes in recoveries were $111,043 against $63,636. The 10-K attributes over-performance to new technologies and digital capabilities that reach more consumers.
quotes: The collections over-performance in the U.S. was driven by the deployment of new technologies, enhanced digital capabilities and continued operational innovation, which enabled us to reach more consumers, leading to more payments as well as a larger payer book.

growth_thesis.basis: Figures are stated in F2; the condition is inferred from F2 and the risk factor in P2.
growth_thesis.claim: Operating leverage supports profit growth, and it depends on costs growing more slowly than revenue. Third-quarter total revenues were 544,541 (table in thousands) against 460,353, while total operating expenses were 313,936 against 287,175. Cost of legal collections rose to 100,400 from 80,010. For the margin gain to continue, legal-channel costs must not outrun the collections they generate.
quotes: As we increase our use of the legal channel for collections, our short-term margins may decrease as a result of an increase in upfront court costs and costs related to counter claims.

growth_thesis.basis: Figures are stated in F1, F3 and P4; the dependence on funding is inferred from the balance sheet and cash flow pattern and P1's stated strategy.
growth_thesis.claim: Debt funding access is a condition for the growth. Borrowings were 4,237,800 (table in thousands) against 4,001,293 at year-end. Nine-month purchases were $1,196,311, while net cash provided by operating activities was 159,630. Continued purchasing therefore depends on refinancing and borrowing on acceptable terms.
quotes: Depending on the capital markets, we may consider additional financings to refinance debt or fund our operations and any potential acquisitions.

growth_thesis.basis: Share counts, EPS and repurchase amounts are stated in F2 and P6; the leverage condition is stated in P1.
growth_thesis.claim: Share repurchases add to per-share growth. Diluted weighted shares fell to 22,255 (table in thousands) from 23,520 in the third quarter, and diluted EPS was $5.57 against $3.17. The company repurchased approximately $27 million in the quarter and approximately $73 million over nine months. For this to continue, leverage must stay within or below the target range and excess cash must not be needed elsewhere.
quotes: we may allocate capital toward share repurchases

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P6; the conditions are inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Management has raised full-year guidance on the strength of the above drivers. It now expects global purchases between $1.50 billion and $1.55 billion, collections between $2.90 billion and $2.95 billion, and EPS between $15.50 and $16.00. This holds only if U.S. supply, pricing and collections performance persist through year-end.
quotes: Given the strength and momentum of our business, we are raising our full-year 2026 guidance.

growth_thesis.claim: Europe is a smaller and less certain contributor. Third-quarter European purchases were $79,702 (table in thousands) against $84,929, and collections were 164,084 against 160,329. Growth there depends on pricing and spot or forward flow timing that the company says constrain its deployment.
quotes: Pricing continues to remain competitive in our European footprint, constraining the amount of capital we choose to deploy in Europe.

risks.basis: inferred from the balance sheet and cash flow statement; the filings excerpted here do not state a liquidity warning
risks.claim: Borrowings rose to 4,237,800 (table in thousands) at Sep. 30, 2026 from 4,001,293 at Dec. 31, 2025, against stockholders' equity of 1,078,682 and cash of 158,425. The company's funding and refinancing needs are therefore large relative to its cash.
quotes: We are focused on strengthening our balance sheet while delivering strong financial and operational results.

risks.basis: stated in the 10-K risk factor and MD&A; the link to Q3 2026 revenue mix is inferred from the income statement
risks.claim: A large share of earnings growth rests on changes in recoveries. These were 111,043 (table in thousands) of 525,457 total debt purchasing revenue in Q3 2026, versus 63,636 a year earlier. If collections over-performance reverses, revenue and earnings would fall.
quotes: We may not be able to achieve the collections forecasted by our models.
We recorded $167.9 million in net negative change in expected future recoveries during the year ended December 31, 2024.

risks.basis: stated in the 10-K risk factor; the quarterly cost trend is read from the income statement
risks.claim: Cost of legal collections rose to 100,400 (table in thousands) in Q3 2026 from 80,010 a year earlier as the legal channel was used more. Rising court costs could compress margins.
quotes: As we increase our use of the legal channel for collections, our short-term margins may decrease as a result of an increase in upfront court costs and costs related to counter claims.

risks.basis: stated in the 10-Q MD&A and the 10-K risk factors; the effect on returns is stated generally, not quantified
risks.claim: Portfolio pricing in the U.S. was slightly higher in Q3 2026 than in prior quarters. Higher prices or competition could lower returns on new purchases, which are central to growth.
quotes: With market supply remaining elevated, pricing in the third quarter remained at favorable levels, although portfolio pricing was slightly higher compared to prior quarters.
Further, our rates of return may decline when portfolio prices are high.

risks.basis: stated in the 10-Q MD&A; the concentration point is inferred from the purchase and collection tables

quotes: Pricing continues to remain competitive in our European footprint, constraining the amount of capital we choose to deploy in Europe.

risks.basis: stated in the 10-K risk factors; no current deterioration is shown in the evidence
risks.claim: The business is exposed to a consumer downturn. A recession could raise bankruptcy filings, which would hurt collections on unsecured receivables.
quotes: Our business model may be uniquely vulnerable to an economic recession, which typically results in an increase in the amount of defaulted consumer receivables, thereby contributing to an increase in the amount of personal bankruptcy filings.

risks.basis: stated in the 10-K risk factor; no specific action appears in the evidence
risks.claim: The business is subject to extensive and growing laws and regulations, so new rules or enforcement could raise costs or limit collection practices.
quotes: Our business is subject to extensive laws and regulations, which have increased and may continue to increase.

unresolved_questions.basis: Inferred from the risk factor and the P&L and collections tables. The Q3 MD&A cost explanation was omitted from the excerpt.
unresolved_questions.claim: Will legal collections costs keep growing faster than other costs? Cost of legal collections was 100,400 (table in thousands) against 80,010 a year earlier, while U.S. legal collections were 219,444 against 170,545.

unresolved_questions.basis: Inferred from the quarterly tables and MD&A text. The causes of the servicing revenue decline are not in the visible evidence.

quotes: In general, portfolio pricing remains competitive across our European footprint, constraining the amount of capital we elect to deploy in Europe.

unresolved_questions.claim: How will management balance debt reduction against buybacks, and where does leverage sit against its target range? Repurchases were 73,993 (table in thousands) over nine months, against borrowings of 4,237,800 and equity of 1,078,682.
quotes: Depending on our relative leverage and a number of other factors, we may apply excess cash toward reducing our debt or, in circumstances in which we are operating within our target leverage range or below the lower end of our target leverage range, we may allocate capital toward share repurchases.

P4.s109.text: Collections from purchased receivables increased by $286.3 million, or 14.9%, to $2,209.1 million during the nine months ended September 30, 2026, as compared to $1,922.8 million during the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

P6.s18.text: We now anticipate global portfolio purchases to be in a range between $1.50 billion and $1.55 billion, and global collections to be in a range between $2.90 billion and $2.95 billion, reflecting year-over-year growth of 12-14%.

P6.s19.text: Additionally, we now expect our EPS in 2026 to be in a range between $15.50 and $16.00 per share, an increase of over 40% compared to 2025.

unknowns: The evidence gives no return-on-equity or book-equity growth guidance, so no guidance option is used.

Full-year 2026 book equity growth is not stated. Equity rose from $976,750 to $1,078,682 (thousands) over nine months, which is above the neutral 3.75%, but the 27.29% last-year figure may overstate it, so the neutral option is kept.
How long the 2025-2026 collections over-performance and high returns will last is not known.
The share of 2026 earnings that comes from recoveries above forecast, which varies from period to period, cannot be separated from the evidence given.

verdict_reason: expected return +2.1 points a year against the required return over 3 years (BUY needs 4 or more)
